review: 1:3 בִּרְצוֹן לֵב — 'with the will of the heart', for بِاخْتِيَارٍ; the noun רָצוֹן with לֵב marks willing consent, which is the doctrine of the stanza (John 10:18).
1:4 וַיִּכְרַע רֹאשׁ יָקָר — 'and the precious head bowed'; the Arabic الْكَرِيم is 'noble', but יָקָר is the word used of the head in Ps 139:17 and fits the metre.
2:1 פָּנֶיךָ בֹּהֲקִים יֹפִי — 'Your face, radiant with beauty'; בֹּהֲק is the rare biblical 'shining' (Ezek 21:10), chosen for the assonance and the five syllables.
3:1 גַּלֵּי אֵל — 'the billows of God' (Jonah 2:4, Ps 42:8); the Arabic تَيَّارَاتُ اللهِ is the same image and the psalm text is kept close.
3:4 נֶחְשַׁבְתָּ תַּחְתֵּנוּ — 'You were reckoned in our place'; the Arabic الْبَدِيل ('substitute') is a doctrinal term, and נֶחְשַׁב is the verb of Isa 53:4 (נֶחְשַׁב כִּמְצֹרָע).
4:4 וַתַּעְנֵק — 'and You gave us peace to enjoy'; the hiph'il of ענק is post-biblical but liturgical-standard, and it fills the line where שָׁלוֹם alone would fall short.
